## Introduction

My data visualization project leverages the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) dataset to answer the question: when did computer science (CS) become such a popular undergraduate degree, and how has its popularity varied geographically and across institutions? 

This question is motivated and informed by my previous data projects I have worked on as part of my job in high education administration. Of course, the "learn-to-code" phenomenon is a ubiquitious topic in higher education, yet I was still surprised to see the dramatic national trend in CS degrees in the dataset. 

Furthermore, as part of my previous IPEDS data project, I struggled to efficiently visualize the rich degrees granted IPEDS dataset. I wanted to maximize the freedom of users to discover trends in the data across institutions. However, many visualizations involved line plots with many institutions shown as different colors, producing a "rainbow spaghetti" effect that obscured trends and likely discouraged exploration. Thus, for this project, I wanted to begin with a more focused question and an improved understanding of effective visualization design from Dr. Albers Szafir's lectures.
